benefits.name: Real Property Tax Exemption for 100% Disabled Veterans
benefits.description: Virginia exempts from local real property tax the principal residence (dwelling plus up to one acre of land) of any veteran rated by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs as 100 percent service-connected, permanent, and total. An unmarried surviving spouse of a qualifying veteran who died on or after January 1, 2011 may continue to receive the exemption.
benefits.value: 100% exemption from local real property tax on the qualifying dwelling and up to 1 acre of land

otherReqs: Property must be occupied as the veteran's principal place of residence
Applies for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2011

documentation: VA Summary of Benefits letter showing 100% service-connected, permanent, and total disability

benefits.name: Personal Property Tax Exemption for One Vehicle (100% Disabled Veterans)
benefits.description: One motor vehicle (passenger car, pickup, or panel truck registered for personal use) owned and used primarily by a 100 percent service-connected, permanent, and total disabled veteran is exempt from local personal property tax. For married couples, either spouse holding the qualifying rating makes the vehicle eligible. The exemption ends when the veteran dies and does not carry over to a surviving spouse.
benefits.value: 100% exemption from local personal property tax on one qualifying vehicle

otherReqs: Applies to only one vehicle per veteran
Vehicle must be a passenger car, pickup, or panel truck registered for personal use
Exemption expires on the veteran's death; does not pass to a surviving spouse

documentation: VA rating decision or Summary of Benefits letter showing 100% service-connected, permanent, and total disability

benefits.name: Virginia Military Survivors and Dependents Education Program (VMSDEP)
benefits.description: VMSDEP waives tuition and mandatory fees for up to eight semesters at a Virginia public college, university, or Eastern Virginia Medical School for the spouse or a child (ages 16-29) of a veteran who has been rated by the U.S. VA as totally and permanently disabled, or at least 90 percent permanently disabled, due to service, and discharged under conditions other than dishonorable (also available to survivors of service members killed, missing in action, or POW). Domicile/residency conditions apply to the qualifying service member. A separate stipend fund exists under Va. Code § 23.1-608.1, which was not independently verified in this research.
benefits.value: Full waiver of tuition and mandatory fees for up to 8 semesters (4 academic years) at a Virginia public institution of higher education

otherReqs: Beneficiary is the spouse or a child aged 16-29 of the qualifying veteran or service member
Veteran discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable

Qualifying service member/veteran must meet Virginia domicile requirements (e.g., established residency at time of entering active service, or 5 years' physical presence in Virginia prior to application)

documentation: VA rating decision showing total/permanent disability or at least 90% permanent disability

benefits.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plates
benefits.description: Veterans with a service-connected disability certified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs may obtain special red/white/blue 'DV' license plates. One set of Disabled Veteran or standard passenger special plates is provided at no cost to a veteran who has lost, or lost the use of, a limb, is blind, or is permanently and totally disabled (and to their un-remarried surviving spouse); other service-connected disabled veterans may purchase the DV plate design. The disabled (International Symbol of Access) version requires additional medical certification.
benefits.value: Special DV-design license plate; free for veterans who lost/lost use of a limb, are blind, or are permanently and totally disabled

otherReqs: Certification from the U.S. VA that the disability is service-connected
Free set of plates limited to veterans who lost/lost use of a limb, are blind, or are permanently and totally disabled (or their un-remarried surviving spouse)

application.form: VSA 10 (License Plate Application); VSA 54 (Veteran Certification of Disability)
documentation: Form VSA 54 signed by a veteran service officer, or a U.S. VA benefit letter

benefits.name: Vehicle Registration Fee Waiver for Disabled Veterans
benefits.description: No annual DMV registration fee is required for one motor vehicle owned and used personally by a veteran whose disability has been certified as service-connected by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. This waiver applies alongside (but is distinct from) the DV license plate program.
benefits.value: Annual vehicle registration fee waived for one qualifying vehicle

otherReqs: Certification from the U.S. VA that the disability is service-connected
Limited to one motor vehicle owned and used personally by the veteran

documentation: Form VSA 54 or U.S. VA benefit letter certifying service-connected disability

benefits.name: Veterans Preference in Commonwealth State Employment
benefits.description: Veterans, their surviving spouses, and children receive hiring preference for Commonwealth of Virginia state government jobs. For positions using a numerically scored assessment, 5 percentage points are added to a veteran's passing score, or 10 points for a veteran with a service-connected disability rating fixed by the U.S. VA. For non-exam-based hiring, qualifying veterans, surviving spouses, or children are given preference in the selection process provided they meet all knowledge, skill, and ability requirements.
benefits.value: 5-point score preference on scored exams (10 points for service-connected disabled veterans); preference in non-exam hiring

otherReqs: Honorable discharge and more than 180 consecutive days of full-time active-duty service, OR a service-connected disability rating fixed by the U.S. VA
Must meet all knowledge, skill, and ability requirements for the position

application.agency: Virginia Department of Human Resource Management (DHRM)
documentation: VA disability rating letter, if claiming disability-based preference

benefits.name: Virginia Veterans Care Centers
benefits.description: The Virginia Department of Veterans Services operates state veterans care centers providing skilled nursing, dementia/memory care, and short-term rehabilitative care, statutorily authorized as part of DVS's responsibility for 'medical care centers...for veterans owned and operated by the Commonwealth.' Publicly known locations include Sitter & Barfoot (Richmond), Davis & McDaniel (Roanoke), and Jones & Cabacoy (Virginia Beach), with a fourth (Puller, Fauquier County) reported as under construction. This research could not independently confirm the specific admission criteria (discharge type, minimum service length, income/means testing) or payer details because DVS's dedicated care-center and eligibility pages returned an access-blocked (HTTP 403) response on every direct fetch attempt; contact DVS or a specific care center to confirm current admission requirements before relying on any percentage or dollar figure.
